It's been really affecting my ability to move my arm and even my sleep. Doctor: Can you describe the nature of the shoulder pain (e.g., sharp, dull, burning) and whether it radiates to other areas? Have you experienced any associated symptoms such as chest pain, shortness of breath, or arm numbness? Do you have a history of trauma to the shoulder or any prior medical conditions such as heart disease, diabetes, or rheumatoid arthritis? Patient: The pain is more of a dull, aching sensation, and it stays right around my shoulder—it doesn’t go anywhere else. I haven’t had any chest pain, shortness of breath, or numbness in my arm. As for trauma, I don’t remember hitting it or falling, but I have been doing a lot of work in my basement lately, like putting in a new ceiling. I don’t have any of those medical conditions you mentioned. Doctor: Have you experienced any swelling, redness, or warmth around the left shoulder? Have you noticed any limitation in the range of motion or weakness in the arm? Patient: I haven't noticed any swelling, redness, or warmth around my shoulder. I do have a lot of trouble moving my arm, especially when I try to lift anything or reach overhead—it causes a lot of pain, and I’ve been avoiding those movements altogether.
